key_insight: HTP-Net improves instance segmentation of dense, slender welding material stubs by preserving boundaries, modeling long-range topology, and using orientation-aware predictions.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stub counting and shape measurement can support welding-factory inventory management.
method: Wavelet-driven edge preservation retains fine boundaries during feature downsampling.
Long-range topology modeling reduces segmentation breaks in slender targets.
An orientation-driven segmentation head addresses excessive non-maximum suppression and overlapping masks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mAP50 gains of 1.2%–55.3% over existing methods on custom and public datasets, plus factory-deployed average recognition accuracies of 99% for electrode stubs and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify inference speed or robustness across different factory lighting, cameras, and material arrangements.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
